standard.title: Investigate choreographers and meaning
standard.description: investigate performers' and/or choreographers' use of elements of dance, choreographic devices, genre- or style-specific techniques, conventions and/or production elements to communicate and/or challenge ideas, perspectives and/or meaning in dance across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can investigate dance works, performers and/or choreographers across cultures, times, places and contexts (Y7-8, AC9ADA8E01). They can analyse element and device use, investigate digital tool influence, and evaluate choreographic intent.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students investigate performers' and/or choreographers' use of elements, devices, genre/style-specific techniques, conventions and/or production elements to communicate and/or challenge ideas, perspectives and/or meaning across cultures, times, places and/or other contexts.

nodes.label: Investigating choreographic practice in context
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can investigate how and why choreographers and performers work within specific cultural, social, historical and environmental contexts — analysing how context shapes practice.
nodes.minimum_width: Investigating one choreographer or dance practitioner — connecting their contextual position (cultural, historical, social) to at least two identifiable choices in their work.
nodes.typical_width: Investigating how and why choreographers work with communities to advocate for social justice or sustainable living; exploring specific examples of practitioners working with communities in Australia with cultural links to Asia; analysing how traditions, styles and contexts affect experience and interpretation; extending own movement vocabulary through analysis of others' stylistic preferences.
wider: Investigate a choreographer whose practice is grounded in a specific cultural community — analysing how community context shapes every aspect of the work
Compare how two choreographers from different cultural or historical contexts address the same theme — analysing how context determines approach, form and reception
nodes.hinge_reason: Context-driven analysis — understanding why a choreographer made specific choices given their position — is the analytical depth that distinguishes investigating from describing. Students without this move cannot engage critically with cultural diversity or social justice in dance.

response_modes.reason: Contextual analysis requires an explicit methodology — teach students to move from 'what I see' to 'why this choice, given this context'. Use a structured inquiry model: context → choice → effect → interpretation.
Investigating practitioners across genuinely diverse cultural, temporal and geographic contexts builds analytical range and prevents single-tradition dominance of the student's interpretive frame.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Students who investigate choreographic practice across diverse contexts develop cultural-analytical literacy that serves them as practitioners, audience members and citizens — extending well beyond dance.
success_criteria: Student connects at least two choreographic choices to the practitioner's contextual position (cultural, social, historical)
Student can articulate how context shapes the way a dance communicates or challenges ideas

nodes.label: Personal identity and stylistic development
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use investigation of diverse dance styles and genres to inform and develop their own stylistic preferences and personal choreographic identity.
nodes.minimum_width: Analysing element use in at least one genre/style they have not previously worked in — identifying one way it could inform their own practice.
nodes.typical_width: Extending movement vocabulary as they explore own stylistic preferences and personal identity; using analysis of dance styles from cultures they identify with or from different times to inform choreographic practice; analysing element use in popular culture styles or styles from Asia as stimulus.
wider: Develop a personal style statement — articulating the choreographic influences, cultural references and aesthetic preferences that shape their dance identity
Investigate how a dance style from a country or region in Asia has been adopted, adapted or appropriated in Western contexts — using this analysis to inform respectful practice

response_modes.reason: Style development integrates contextual investigation (N1) with personal identity and creative practice. The key move is from 'I analysed this style' to 'and here is what it does for my work'.

success_criteria: Student analyses element use in at least one unfamiliar genre/style
Student can explain how this analysis informs or challenges their own choreographic or performance practice
